title: vulnerability research just got easier (scarier?)
summary: A security engineer walks through how OpenAI's o3 found a Linux kernel SMB use-after-free zero-day, stressing its high false-positive rate and how much context size matters.

assertions.quote: the chance of getting correct results is sufficiently high that it is worth your time and your effort to try to use on real problems

verdicts.note: By 2025-26 AI systems (Big Sleep, AIxCC entrants, lab red-team reports) found many confirmed real vulnerabilities, though false positives remain common and human triage is still needed.

assertions.quote: in the remaining 28 of the reports, there are false positives

verdicts.note: Documented across curl's public HackerOne reports and other projects: fabricated stack traces, nonexistent functions, already-fixed CVEs.

assertions.quote: 03 finds the Keraros off bug one out of 100 times with this larger number of input tokens.

verdicts.note: Long-context benchmarks (e.g. NoLiMa, context-rot studies) show degradation as context grows; the exact threshold is model-dependent.

assertions.quote: You're giving it like random utility functions that like the user can't even access.

verdicts.note: As models improved, output depends more on relevant, high-signal context than phrasing; consistent with Anthropic/Cursor guidance and long-context degradation evidence.

assertions.quote: there's a lot of AI generated bug reports that are just not correct that is basically clogging up the machine

verdicts.note: curl's public data and statements from other maintainers (Python, Django, FFmpeg) document a sharp rise in fabricated AI reports; curl ended its bug bounty in 2026 partly because of it.

assertions.quote: it had realized that setting session user equal to null was insufficient to fix the issue

verdicts.note: Maintainers widely report poor auto-fixes, and fix quality lags detection in evaluations; but auto-fix quality has improved and varies by bug type.
